prompts.fpv:
Create ONE production-ready 2D pixel-art sprite atlas for the game GREYLINE. The reference image is STYLE ONLY, not an edit target. It shows the desired muted olive realistic military pixel language. New subject: a compact first-person-view quadcopter, visibly four small propellers on a low dark carbon frame, olive battery shell, tiny forward camera; realistic proportions, NOT a toy, NOT a helicopter, no people, no text, no technical diagrams. True sharply stepped pixel clusters, clean silhouette, no blurry painted edges. Side view facing RIGHT. Small enough that the game will display it around 54 by 28 pixels. Keep recognizable compact body with thin short rotor arms; no huge wings or helicopter tail.
Atlas exactly 4 columns x 2 rows, equal 384x384 cells on a 1536x768 transparent canvas. Generous empty margins, no element crossing cell boundaries. All cells consistent identical object scale.
TOP ROW: four level-flight animation frames of the SAME drone body centered at the SAME pixel coordinate. The rigid body MUST remain absolutely identical in every frame; only the propeller blade silhouettes change through four distinct rotation phases. No camera movement or pitch bob.
BOTTOM ROW: four views/stages of the SAME destroyed FPV drone grounded on a common baseline: (1) freshly broken drone with one snapped rotor arm, (2) drone on its side with broken props, (3) settled charred compact frame with loose small fragments close around it, (4) alternate settled wreck with exposed compact frame. These are independently drawn wreck sprites, never squash a whole aircraft. No fire, no smoke, no ground plane, no shadows extending far away.
Transparent alpha background, NOT checkerboard drawn into RGB, no labels or gridlines. Crisp production sprites, desaturated military palette.
prompts.cards:
Generate one 2-panel art sheet with EXACTLY TWO SQUARE military unit promotional illustrations arranged side-by-side, same scale, no gap. Overall 2:1 landscape. Use the supplied command vehicle card image only as the STYLE REFERENCE: same muted olive/khaki and warm gray military propaganda/catalog illustration treatment, subtle grain, realistic adult proportions, realistic materials, dramatic reserved lighting, coherent collectible card art direction. This is publicity/hero unit artwork, NOT in-game deployed unit photographs or screenshots, NOT a colorful toy, NOT a comic, NOT pixel sprites. Both images should work inside the same existing card frame. No frame or border, NO text, NO letters, NO labels, NO logos, no numbers, no signature.
LEFT SQUARE: promotional hero image of a compact military FPV quadcopter, low-angle closeup hanging in the air above a weathered crate, dark carbon low frame and four small propellers, olive central battery case and tiny forward camera; a helmeted operator in softly out-of-focus background holding a radio controller, looking purposeful, distant field trees and gray sky. Drone is the unmistakable focus, not a large helicopter or sci-fi machine. No visible construction detail or schematic.
RIGHT SQUARE: promotional hero portrait of a helicopter assault infantry squad, three adult modern soldiers in olive field kit and helmets, natural long adult anatomy, posed confidently on an airstrip, foreground squad leader chest-to-thigh and two soldiers behind; transport helicopter behind them with open side doorway and rotor, low-angle composition under the same restrained overcast light. The image should sell a trained rapid air assault unit; not depicting an attack or actual combat.
Keep both pictures equally finished, same contrast and palette as reference, each fills its own square with center-safe focal subject, a clean seam exactly at half width, no subjects straddling panels.
prompts.maps:
Create one pixel-art background atlas for GREYLINE 2D side-scrolling military game. Reference image is STYLE AND CAMERA REFERENCE ONLY, not edit target. EXACTLY THREE horizontal panoramic landscape panels stacked vertically with NO gutters, NO borders and NO text. Overall canvas square, each panel exactly width:height 3:1. Each row is a DIFFERENT biome background, uniform rendering style and pixels.
Authentic crisp game pixel art: stepped pixel clusters, restricted desaturated palette, no smooth painting, no photoreal photography, no blur. Match reference's late-1990s realistic war game pixel environment. Side-on low viewpoint looking across flat far distance. These are BACKDROPS, not walkable foreground: do not include foreground tree trunks, front fences, large near houses, giant foreground rocks or occluding cover. Trees/buildings must look distinctly far away with atmospheric lighter values. The real ground and collision objects will be drawn separately. Reserve upper 60 percent of EACH panel as open sky with restrained pixel cloud layers for aircraft visibility. Scenic horizon silhouettes start around 60 percent down, low distant environment occupies bottom 40 percent. Bottom boundary should be muted natural biome color, not bright white. No soldiers, vehicles, fighting, explosion, flames, smoke, interface, lettering. Each panorama should be suitable for horizontal repeating background: closely matched scenery color and horizon height at left/right boundaries, no abrupt discontinuities, subtle variation through center.
ROW 1 top: humid JUNGLE, deep moss/olive green palette; distant broadleaf canopy and palms, low misty ridge in graygreen haze, one tiny far ruined outpost roof barely visible. Gray warm humid overcast sky, wide calm composition.
ROW 2 middle: MOUNTAINS, cool slate gray blue palette; layered distant mountain ridges with small snowy high tips and low pine tree line, tiny far mountain hamlet. Mountains rise from bottom into middle distance but preserve generous open sky; no huge foreground mountain blocking most of panel. Cloudy cool daylight.
ROW 3 bottom: DESERT, muted ocher sand and brown palette; distant flat mesas, very low dune ridges, sparse small dry shrubs, one tiny distant adobe settlement, dusty pale sky. Natural austere scene, not bright orange cartoon.
Every panel equally sharp and equally pixelated, compatible horizon and altitude, coherent serious military aesthetic.

postprocess: Only image crops, resizing, and neutral checker-to-alpha import cleanup. No subjects were drawn procedurally.
